A_general.open_code_note: No official repository or package was found in the prepared evidence. The hosted server is documented on CoinDesk's own endpoint page; implementation equivalence cannot be assessed.
other_official_servers: CoinDesk announced availability through Gemini Enterprise for Financial Services; the announcement does not document a distinct endpoint or tool set.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The MCP page requests an API key and a CoinDesk data license but does not state a price for MCP access. CoinDesk's API license describes subscription fees and licensed data, without publishing prices on the checked pricing page.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: A CoinDesk data license and API key are required. The accessed pricing page did not expose readable plan or price details.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The API license says the user selects subscribed data and a subscription period; fees and access limits can depend on the licensed data. No MCP per-call charge or MCP-specific limit was found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: OAuth authentication is required. The user enters a CoinDesk API key during authorization. The CoinDesk API license may limit API requests, sockets, or data accessed. No MCP-specific rate limit was found.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: CoinDesk controls OAuth/API access and licensing; the account holder selects licensed data and subscription period.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The official page lists 39 market-data and news tools across spot, indices, futures, options, news, and on-chain data. It does not publish schemas, tool annotations, or tool descriptions beyond names and example prompts.
The public endpoint documentation does not describe MCP resources. No public server code or unauthenticated endpoint response was available to verify support.
The endpoint page provides example user queries, but does not identify them as MCP prompts or document a prompts/list interface.
No MCP request logging, audit trail, or telemetry behavior is documented in the checked MCP materials.
No sampling capability is documented in the endpoint page or available public code.
No roots capability is documented in the endpoint page or available public code.

A POST to the endpoint returned HTTP 401 with a Bearer challenge referencing the protected-resource metadata URL. That metadata identifies the same-host authorization server. Its authorization-server metadata advertises authorization-code and refresh-token grants, S256 PKCE, dynamic client registration, and no supported scopes. OpenID configuration and the path-suffixed protected-resource metadata URL returned 404.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: OAuth authorization endpoints are advertised at /authorize and /token; registration is advertised at /register. The endpoint response without a token is HTTP 401.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration. Raw metadata: protected resource HTTP 200: {"resource":"https://mcp.coindesk.com/mcp","authorization_servers":["https://mcp.coindesk.com"]}. Authorization server HTTP 200: {"authorization_endpoint":"https://mcp.coindesk.com/authorize","code_challenge_methods_supported":["S256"],"grant_types_supported":["authorization_code","refresh_token"],"issuer":"https://mcp.coindesk.com","registration_endpoint":"https://mcp.coindesk.com/register","response_types_supported":["code"],"scopes_supported":[],"token_endpoint":"https://mcp.coindesk.com/token","token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported":["client_secret_post","client_secret_basic"]}. Token lifetime and revocation are not stated in the provided metadata. The official setup page says users enter their CoinDesk API key during authentication.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The setup flow requires users to enter an API key in a browser, but the documentation does not characterize this OAuth interaction as MCP elicitation.
No MCP tasks support is documented.

The endpoint page provides client-specific connection setup for Claude CLI/Desktop and Gemini CLI. It documents the global endpoint URL and OAuth flow, but no server URL parameters, request headers, tool filters, or runtime configuration options.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: No MCP-specific error reporting interface or error format is documented. The unauthenticated endpoint response is HTTP 401.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: The endpoint returned HTTP 401 without a bearer token; other MCP error formats are unknown.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: No MCP subscription capability is documented. API data access is subject to a selected data license and subscription period, which is a commercial access arrangement rather than documented MCP subscription support.
No MCP progress notification behavior is documented.
No request cancellation behavior is documented.
No initialize instructions or additional MCP capabilities are publicly reproduced. The endpoint page describes a hosted integration for market-data queries and example natural-language prompts.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official list names query tools for market data and news; it publishes no annotations. These are characterized as data-fetching tools, but server-enforced read-only behavior is not independently verified. 2. No server-enforced confirmation, preview/confirm, or approval flow is documented. OAuth/API-key entry is an authentication step, not documented per-call confirmation. 3. OAuth metadata advertises authorization code, refresh tokens, S256 PKCE, dynamic registration, and empty scopes_supported. The setup requires a CoinDesk API key. Inherited product roles, admin switches, redirect approval, token lifetime, and revocation are not documented. 4. The official page gives one global endpoint; no tool filtering, read-only mode, or sandbox endpoint is documented. 5. No MCP-specific PII masking or field-level data protection is described. The API license restricts use and sharing of licensed data. 6. No MCP limits, quotas, or result truncation are published. The API license permits limitations on API requests, sockets, and data volume. 7. Tool schemas and validation/correction behavior are not published; no public code was found. 8. MCP logging, audit trails, and telemetry details were not found in checked sources. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, report, or upsell tool is named in the official list. 10. The public page gives examples but no server-delivered skills or behavioral instructions to the agent. 11. No persistent MCP memory or state behavior is documented. 12. The documented product is a hosted CoinDesk Data & Indices MCP endpoint; no sub-server architecture is described. 13. No raw API, SQL, script execution, or other unrestricted escape-hatch tool is named in the official tool list.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool list exists at https://mcp.coindesk.com/ and names 39 tools; no official total is stated. actions.json contains all 39 official names. No catalogue-only actions were added. The Anthropic Claude connector directory is publisher-verified and lists 24 tools; it uses fetch_spot_orderbook, fetch_futures_orderbook, and fetch_options_orderbook where CoinDesk's official list instead names metrics and snapshot variants, and omits several official tools. Skills Playground also reports 24 and repeats the Claude-style subset. Manufact reports 24 but its captured page only exposes a partial set. MCP.so reports no tool list. Catalogues are cross-checks, not replacements for the official list.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public server code or verbatim complete tool definitions/initialize instructions were available. Names alone are insufficient to serialize tool definitions and calculate the requested estimate.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: A licensed human user can access CoinDesk API data under the selected subscription and license. The API license imposes contractual use, sharing, and security restrictions. The MCP page does not publish the full API operation catalog or enough MCP schemas to identify specific API operations available to humans but absent from MCP.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The page provides example natural-language queries and setup guidance, including “In the browser window that opens, enter your API key to complete authentication.” These are client/user setup instructions; no MCP-side behavioral recommendations to the agent are documented.
F_documentation.governance_promises: No MCP-specific promises about data retention, model training, or audit logging were found. The API license limits use of licensed data, generally to internal use and subject to additional terms. It states that licensed data must be deleted after termination except where retained for legal, regulatory, or audit obligations.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: CoinDesk describes the connector as providing real-time and historical digital asset market data, including spot, derivatives, indices, on-chain data, and news. The announcement states that a CoinDesk data license and API key are required.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The published materials describe access and licensing, but do not expose server code or enough implementation detail to verify enforcement of contractual data-use restrictions, retention, or access limits within MCP.

contradictions: CoinDesk's official list names fetch_spot_orderbook_metrics and fetch_spot_orderbook_snapshot (and corresponding futures/options tools), while the publisher-verified Claude directory lists fetch_spot_orderbook, fetch_futures_orderbook, and fetch_options_orderbook. These are different names and do not establish whether the actions overlap or reflect different versions.
Official list count is 39; Claude directory and Skills Playground report 24. Catalogues omit official tools, so actions.json follows the official list.
observations_for_research: The OAuth server metadata advertises dynamic client registration and an empty supported-scopes list; the endpoint page separately describes entry of a CoinDesk API key during the OAuth authorization flow.
The official documentation exposes more granular orderbook metrics and snapshot tools than the 24-tool Claude directory listing.
notes: Checked the prepared links.json, links_check.txt, pages/INDEX.txt, official endpoint page and its captured HTML/text, pricing and legal pages, OAuth metadata provided in the prompt, and all captured tool-catalogue pages. No official repository, package, tool schemas, or initialize instructions were found. The pricing page capture had no readable text. The Feluda listing returned 404 and was not used. actions.json has 39 official tool names; parameters are marked NOT PUBLISHED because the official source does not provide schemas. The tool descriptions in actions.json are concise summaries inferred from official names and surrounding product descriptions, not verbatim official descriptions.
